chunks: He ordered him to fear Allah in the secrets of his affairs and the hidden aspects of his actions, where there is no witness except Him, and no one watches save Him.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to have taqwa in secret matters according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi presents this instruction as a cornerstone of administrative ethics in Shia thought, urging the official to internalize *taqwa* beyond mere public compliance. It highlights the concept of *ikhlas* (sincerity), where the ruler’s accountability to Allah transcends human observation, ensuring integrity even in the absence of witnesses.
